original_question: If Q_pi(lambda; kappa) denotes the polynomial family arising from the low-rank closure relations and P_pi(lambda, kappa) denotes the family from the high-rank closure relations, does the identity Q_pi(lambda; kappa) = P_pi(lambda, kappa - lambda + pi) hold for every admissible lambda, kappa, and pi?
target_in_paper: Section 10, Conjecture 2: the conjectured change-of-variables relation between the low-rank closure polynomials Qπ and the high-rank closure polynomials Pπ, foreshadowed in the Introduction and defined using the closure relations of Sections 8 and 10.
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the right two polynomial families, distinguishes the low-rank and high-rank closure relations, and asks exactly about the shifted-variable identity that the paper singles out as its Conjecture 2.
missing_details: The paper is not treating Pπ and Qπ as abstract scalar-valued polynomials only in λ and κ: they are closure polynomials depending implicitly on the osp(1|2) tensor-operator parameters c0 and d0 (more precisely on d0 and c0+d0²), while λ and κ are rank parameters.
Pπ is defined by the high-rank closure relation in Section 8, Eq. (8.1), not merely by a name; Qπ is defined by the low-rank closure relation in Section 10, Eq. (10.1).
For the low-rank family the paper assumes κ ≥ λ 'for convenience' in Eq. (10.1); the conjecture is stated in that parametrization.
The admissible ranks are osp(1|2) tensor ranks, hence integral or half-integral values; π also moves in half-integer steps.

The admissible range of π is inherited from the output rank c. In set A, c=λ+κ−π must satisfy c∈[sup(λ,κ), λ+κ]. In set B, c=κ−λ+π must satisfy c∈[|κ−λ|, sup(λ,κ)−1/2]; when κ≥λ this becomes 0≤π≤λ−1/2, with λ≥1/2.

The exact closure formulas also involve the normalization factor E(a,b;c), the supertriangle ▽S(a b c), and, in the low-rank case, an ordered product of γ-coefficients; these are part of the definitions of the Pπ- and Qπ-families in context.
Section 8 records the symmetry Pπ(λ,κ)=Pπ(κ,λ), which is part of the nearby notation and motivation.
Section 8 also gives the coefficient expansion Pπ(λ,κ)=(d0)^τπ Σ_{m=0}^{[π]} x_m^π(λ,κ) (c0+d0²)^[π]-m (d0²)^m, so the coefficient functions x_m^π are implicit in the notation around the conjecture.
The paper states the identity as a conjecture, not a theorem; the nearby evidence is the explicitly recognized π=1/2 case in Section 9, Eq. (9.7).

Appendix B is the technical place where the recursion relations for Pπ and Qπ are listed, so a fully stand-alone version should mention that these families are the ones determined by those closure relations and recursions.
refined_question: In the osp(1|2) intrinsic tensor-operator framework of Sections 8–10, let Pπ(λ,κ) denote the high-rank closure polynomial in the implicit variables d0 and c0+d0² defined by Eq. (8.1), namely by the factor multiplying S_{λ+κ−π} in the closure relation [S_λ × S_κ]_{λ+κ−π}, and let, for κ≥λ≥1/2, Qπ(λ;κ) denote the low-rank closure polynomial defined by Eq. (10.1), namely by the factor multiplying S_{κ−λ+π} in [S_λ × S_κ]_{κ−λ+π}; here λ, κ, π are integral or half-integral ranks and π is restricted so that κ−λ+π lies in the allowed low-rank range [|κ−λ|, κ−1/2] (equivalently 0≤π≤λ−1/2 when κ≥λ). Is it true, as Conjecture 2 asserts, that for every such admissible λ, κ, and π one has Qπ(λ;κ)=Pπ(λ,κ−λ+π)?
justification: The draft is targeting the paper's Conjecture 2 almost verbatim. The Introduction explicitly says that Sections 9–10 introduce polynomials Qπ together with the conjectural relation Qπ(λ,κ)=Pπ(λ,κ−λ+π). Section 8 defines the high-rank family Pπ through the closure relation for [S_λ×S_κ]_{λ+κ−π}, while Section 10 defines the low-rank family Qπ through the closure relation for [S_λ×S_κ]_{κ−λ+π} and then states Conjecture 2 in the exact shifted-variable form. Section 9 supplies the nearby concrete evidence: the π=1/2 low-rank formula is explicitly recognized as the polynomial P_{1/2} after the change κ↦κ−λ+1/2. So the closest paper-faithful stand-alone version is simply Conjecture 2, augmented with the hidden domain restrictions inherited from the defining closure relations.
